cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Will you back 'collecting chairs' when the caretaker asks why we opened the props cupboard? We need him to lend us the hall again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Checking for folding stools, then. Can you back that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you admit you borrowed his key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Borrowed his key to check for extra seating. Will you sign the hall request with me?

cardFidelity.evidence: B2 corrects A's impossible chairs, while A3 merely adds a condescending claim before accepting the correction. S03 is not convincingly driving A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cupboard size causes A3 stools; B4 key admission causes A5 expanded account. The standard prefix contradicts who just supplied the expertise.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects plausibility and B4 insists on admitting key use; B is an active negotiator.

heightening.evidence: A5 incorporates B4 disclosure condition and asks for joint hall paperwork, developing D124 consent.

specificity.evidence: A1 names the cupboard, caretaker and renewed hall use, making the cover story's purpose legible.
